title: astragalus angustiflorus subsp. amanus
intro: Astragalus angustiflorus subsp. amanus, commonly known as a plant species in the Fabaceae family, is a type of legume native to the Mediterranean region. This plant has been traditionally used in medicine for its health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and immunomodulatory effects. The bioactive constituents of Astragalus angustiflorus subsp. amanus include flavonoids, saponins, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its therapeutic actions such as anti-bacterial, anti-viral, and anti-cancer properties. The plant's bioactive constituents have been reported to have potential therapeutic actions, including anti-inflammatory, anti-oxidative, and anti-apoptotic effects, making it a subject of interest in modern medicine.
